cognate: Ved. patnī ~ Gk πότνια (*pótnih₂ 'mistress, lady'); Ved. devī ~ Gk δῖα (both *dyew-/deyw- derivatives, not the identical suffix formation)
drift_or_renewal: Greek θεά (θεάων, πότνα θεά) renews the noun 'goddess'; δῖος survives only as the epithet 'divine, shining'
shared_syntax: title *pótnih₂ + 'divine' epithet in apposition, naming or addressing a female divinity (AV: vocative patni ... devī; Od.: nominative πότνι(α) ... δῖα θεάων)
context: AV 3.12.11 addresses the presiding goddess of the house (śālā) as mistress of the dwelling, sheltering, kindly, a goddess set up by the gods; AVP 19.1.17 calls on goddesses who are mistresses of men; Od. 1.14 names the nymph Calypso as lady and divine among goddesses (Hesiod fr. 150.31 likewise calls her a πότνια nymph). Both AV 3.12.11 and Od. 1.14 concern female numina of a dwelling or holding place (the house-goddess; the nymph who keeps Odysseus in her cave). The automatic match śaraṇa ~ Καλυψώ (both mapped to *ḱel- 'cover') is probably chance and is not part of the claim. Caveats: the patnī ~ πότνια equation and its use as a divine title, including with a dependent genitive (Vedic 'mistress of X' as in AV 3.12.11 and AVŚ 7.47.3; Greek πότνια θηρῶν), is standard (recalled). The co-occurrence with the 'divine' epithet is frequent in Vedic but only twice in Homer (Il. 6.305, Od. 1.14), where δῖα θεάων is an independent stock formula, so the Greek pairing may be an accidental combination of two separate epithets.
phrase: *pótnih₂ + *deyw-/diw- epithet of a goddess (Ved. patnī ... devī ~ Gk πότνια ... δῖα)

words.etymon: pie-lex-h1sumenexs h₁sumenēs (context line: 'pratyaṅ naḥ sumanā bhava')

cognate: Ved. sumánas- ~ Gk εὐμενής (*h₁su-menes- 'well-minded'; also Av. humanah-), with Gk δυσμενής (*dus-menes-) as the antonym
drift_or_renewal: none in the compound; the copula varies (Ved. bhū/as, Gk εἶναι/γίγνεσθαι)
shared_syntax: *h₁su-menes- as predicate of 'be' (Ved. sumanā bhava / asat / bhavantu; Gk εὐμενεῖς εἶναι), said of a being whose goodwill toward a person or group is sought
context: Plato, Laws 927a: the souls of the dead are kindly (εὐμενεῖς) to descendants who honour them and hostile (δυσμενεῖς) to those who dishonour them, i.e. the goodwill of superhuman beings depends on cult. Vedic: in the context line of AVŚ 3.20.4 Agni is asked to be well-minded toward the worshippers (imperative of bhū with sumanā); in AVŚ 3.4.11 and 3.20.12 the same predicate is wished of the king's wives and sons and of the whole people. The Greek poetic parallels in support (H.Hom. 22.7 to Poseidon; Aesch. Eum. 774, of chthonic powers) fit the Vedic prayer use better than the prose anchor does. Caveats: the compound equation (Ved. sumánas-, Av. humanah-, Gk εὐμενής) is standard (recalled); the predicative prayer use is semantically generic and the Greek anchor is prose, so this is at most a weak collocational survival, not a formula.
phrase: *h₁su-menes- *h₁es-/*bʰuH- 'be well-minded (toward)', said of gods and spirits
